Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government digital identity systems and credentials. 30 variables in 5 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Whether the system enables individuals to authenticate themselves or their documents digitally through electronic verification
Comments: No digital authentication function exists in the current ID system. The National Digital Governance Strategy (2020) proposes an Authentication Platform with single sign-on integrated with Digital Identity, but this has not been deployed. The World Bank project targets interoperability and digital services but these are future deliverables. QR codes on the cédula pessoal allow basic offline verification via Leginon, not digital authentication. Scored 1 (No).

Definition: Whether authentication is possible through a centralized government portal or digital gateway
Comments: No government portal using digital ID for authentication was found. The National Digital Governance Strategy (2020) proposes a single government portal (GOV.ST) with ID-based authentication, but the World Bank project status as of Oct 2025 shows interoperability and digital government systems are not yet operational. Scored 1 (No).

Definition: Whether individuals can view their data held in the ID database and see how it has been accessed
Comments: Law 03/2016 grants data subjects the right to access, correct and request deletion of personal data. However, no digital portal or mechanism for individuals to view their own ID data online has been found. Access to personal data records currently requires in-person requests to the DGRN or ANPDP. The National Digital Governance Strategy (2020) proposes future citizen-facing digital services. Scored 1 (No online/digital self-access mechanism).

Definition: Whether the system enables Know Your Customer (KYC) packet collection for service provision, particularly financial services
Comments: The World Bank assessment confirms the national ID card and passport are used for manual KYC in banking (NAP 09/2018 KYC rules). Smile ID confirms STP passport and driver's licence are accepted KYC documents under Law No. 8/13 (AML/KYC). KYC is currently manual (physical document + biometric face match). e-KYC is proposed for future implementation under MOSIP but not yet available. Scored 2 (Yes - manual KYC enabled).

Definition: Whether the ID authority and system are subject to general oversight of the courts and judicial review
Value Name: Yes, but not specific to ID
Comments: STP's constitution and legal system provide general judicial oversight of state actions, including data protection matters. Law 03/2016 allows civil liability claims and provides criminal sanctions enforced through the courts. However, no ID-specific judicial oversight mechanisms have been found. Cybercrime Law 15/2017 includes procedural provisions for courts. Scored 2 (Yes but not ID-specific).

Definition: Whether the civil registration and digital ID systems are integrated
Comments: The DGRN manages both civil registration (SIGA) and the ID system, and ID enrolment reuses SIGA data via QR code/name search. A birth certificate is mandatory for obtaining an ID card. However, the World Bank assessment describes the CR-ID link as 'nascent': there is no automatic update mechanism, data entry remains manual post-SIGA, and no unique identifier (UIN) links the systems. The MOSIP pilot aims to build a fully integrated system. Scored 2 (Partial).

Definition: Whether procedural rules for collection, storage, and sharing of ID-related personal data are publicly available and established
Comments: Law 03/2016 restricts cross-border data transfers, requiring ANPDP authorisation or notification depending on whether the recipient jurisdiction provides adequate protection. The Leginon platform provides controlled institutional access to SIGA data via secure VPN. However, comprehensive data sharing rules for the forthcoming digital ID system are not yet published; the World Bank project targets a data strategy and action plan as an end-project deliverable. Scored 2 (Partially available).

Definition: Whether specific regulation or policy addresses digital ID beyond general identification legislation
Comments: No specific digital ID regulation exists as of 2025. The World Bank Digital STP project (P177158) targets publication of an ID strategy and modernisation roadmap (indicator not yet met as of Oct 2025). The MOSIP pilot is underway but no dedicated digital ID law has been enacted. The National Digital Governance Strategy (2020) includes digital ID as a pillar but is a strategy document, not a regulation. Scored 1 (No).

Definition: Whether national data protection legislation exists and covers personal data linked to the ID system
Comments: Law No. 03/2016 (Personal Data Guarantee and Protection Law), enacted May 10, 2016, establishes a comprehensive data protection framework closely mirroring the EU Data Protection Directive (95/46/EC). It establishes the National Data Protection Agency (ANPDP), defines principles of lawfulness, transparency, proportionality and minimisation, and sets penalties for violations. Scored 2 (Yes).

Definition: Whether a Data Protection Authority or similar body regulates ID data collection and sharing by the ID system
Comments: The National Data Protection Agency (ANPDP - Agência Nacional de Protecção de Dados Pessoais) was established under Law 03/2016. It is operationally active, independently structured, empowered to investigate, subpoena evidence, impose fines, and publish annual reports. The Data Protection Africa fact sheet confirms the ANPDP is 'operational and relatively active in providing authorisations, resolutions, and opinions.' Scored 2 (Yes).

Definition: Whether formal legislation (act, law, regulation) governs digital identity including identification acts, digital ID laws, or equivalent legislation
Comments: A legal framework governing civil identification exists, rooted in colonial-era Decree 251/71 (1971) and updated by Decree 09/2018 on digitisation. The Constitution (Art. 24) protects personal identity. Data Protection Law No. 03/2016 is in force. However, the World Bank assessment notes the laws are outdated and scattered with gaps for digital ID applicability. An ID strategy and modernisation roadmap is planned under World Bank project P177158. Scored 2 (Yes - framework exists but needs modernisation).

Definition: Whether the system and the production of credentials can be managed, maintained and developed by in-country technical staff (as opposed to foreign vendors)
Comments: The World Bank assessment notes that SIGA is hosted in Portugal (University of Aveiro), representing a significant dependency on foreign infrastructure with associated business continuity risks. The DGRN operates the ID database domestically but relies on external vendors for core systems. MOSIP implementation involves international technical assistance. The World Bank Digital STP project aims to build in-country capacity. Scored 2 (Partial in-country).

Definition: Whether the Ministry of Finance has oversight of the financing and development of the digital ID system
Comments: The DGRN (under Ministry of Justice) has administrative and financial autonomy and collects fee revenue from ID issuance. The Ministry of Planning, Finance and Blue Economy (MPFEA) oversees the national budget, including funding for DGRN and the World Bank Digital STP project. The 2019 PEFA assessment confirms MPFEA role in PFM but notes weak oversight of autonomous institutions. No evidence of direct MoF-specific ID financial oversight mechanism. Scored 2 (Partial).

Definition: Whether the ongoing management, maintenance and development of the ID system can be funded by sustainable domestic resources
Comments: The digital ID modernisation effort is primarily funded by external sources: World Bank IDA grant (P177158, USD 16.25M+) and the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation via MOSIP. The World Bank assessment notes DGRN is resource-constrained with only 81 staff (2016), and the SIGA system is hosted externally in Portugal at no disclosed in-country cost. Revenue from ID fees (STN 100-160 per card) is collected but insufficient for full sustainability. Scored 1 (Primarily external).

Definition: Whether the system collects biometric data and which modalities are collected (fingerprints, facial image, iris scans)
Comments: The World Bank foundational ID assessment (2024) confirmed the DGRN ID system collects facial images and fingerprints (index finger, previously 10 fingerprints) for enrolment and renewal. The MOSIP pilot uses TECH5's ABIS (Automated Biometric Identification System) as its foundational layer, supporting both fingerprint and facial biometrics. Scored 3 (Facial/Iris [facial used; iris not confirmed but fingerprint + facial]).

Definition: Whether the country has established or is actively developing a national digital identity system, including foundational ID systems that enable authentication across multiple services. Fully deployed means operational nationwide and accepting new registrations.
Comments: As of June 2025, STP is in an active MOSIP-based digital ID pilot phase. A Justice Ministry representative at ID4Africa 2025 confirmed the pilot is ongoing and progressing well, with nationwide rollout planned within 1-2 years but no fixed timeline set. The existing civil identification system (DGRN/SIGA) is digitised but the new foundational digital ID system is under development, not yet deployed nationwide. Scored 3 (Under development).

Definition: Whether the digital ID system is designed to be interoperable across government agencies and with other systems through APIs or data exchange protocols
Comments: The World Bank Digital STP project (P177158) October 2025 implementation status report confirms the interoperability solution is NOT yet operational (indicator value: No as of Sep 2025, target: Yes by Jun 2027). The existing Leginon layer enables basic SIGA queries via VPN but no comprehensive national interoperability platform exists. Scored 1 (No).

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for opening bank accounts and accessing financial services
Comments: The World Bank assessment confirms that national ID card plus supporting documents (birth certificate, proof of address, parents' documents) are required by banks for account opening under KYC rules (NAP 09/2018). The National Financial Inclusion Strategy targets 70% financial inclusion by 2025. ID is accepted for banking but not mandatory to the exclusion of other documents (passport also accepted). Scored 2 (Accepted, not mandatory as sole document).

Definition: Whether credentials are issued free of charge
Comments: The World Bank assessment documents that ID card issuance costs STN 100 (~USD 4.40) for regular issuance/renewal, STN 130 (~USD 5.80) urgent, and STN 160 (~USD 7.10) very urgent. Birth registration is free if done within 30 days (late registration incurs STN 150 penalty). The credential is NOT free - there is a cost associated with obtaining it. Scored 1 (No [not free]).

Definition: Age in years at which an individual becomes eligible to register for digital ID
Comments: The World Bank assessment indicates the national ID card (bilhete de identidade) is issued to nationals who present a birth certificate. ID enrolment traditionally targets adults; the document notes peak ID issuance occurs just prior to school entry but formal eligibility age for the national ID is not explicitly set below 18. The civil registration (birth certificate) covers all ages including newborns. For the national ID system specifically, eligibility appears to start at 18+. Scored 1 (>17).

Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government digital identity systems and credentials. 30 variables in 5 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Whether registration for digital ID is mandatory, optional, or mandatory for specific groups
Comments: Civil registration (birth, death, marriage) is compulsory under law (births must be registered within 30 days). However, the national ID card itself appears to be optional in practice - the World Bank assessment notes that many adults use the cédula pessoal (birth certificate derivative) and that ID card issuance requires voluntary application at DGRN. No evidence found of mandatory national ID enrollment for adults. Scored 1 (Optional).

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for SIM card activation and mobile service registration
Comments: SIM registration is mandatory in STP under Decree 20/2012. The Prepaid Data SIM Card Wiki confirms: 'Registration is mandatory' at telco-branded stores, requiring ID such as passport. The World Bank assessment confirms ID card/birth certificate/passport plus witnesses are required for SIM registration. Scored 3 (Mandatory).
